literal: Wei Langen; Cui Juan; son Zhan
idiomatic: Wei Langen; Cui Juan; and his son Zhan

literal: Wei Langen was a native of Xiaquyang in Julu.
idiomatic: Wei Langen came from Xiaquyang in Julu Commandery.

literal: His father Bocheng was Administrator of Zhongshan in Wei.
idiomatic: His father Bocheng had served in Wei as administrator of Zhongshan.

literal: Langen was eight chi in height, of striking appearance, broadly read in books, recited the Zuo Tradition and the Book of Changes, quick-witted and perceptive.
idiomatic: Langen stood eight chi tall, with a striking presence. He read widely, knew the Zuo Tradition and Book of Changes by heart, and was quick-witted and perceptive.

literal: He began his career as gentleman-attendant in the princely establishment of the Prince of Beihai, and served successively as senior recorder in Ding Province.
idiomatic: He began as gentleman-attendant in the household of the Prince of Beihai and later served as senior recorder in Ding Province.

literal: When his mother died he observed mourning, and won a reputation for filial piety.
idiomatic: When his mother died he entered mourning and won renown for filial piety.

literal: When the burial was to take place within Changshan Commandery, there stood a shrine to Dong Zhuo beforehand, with a cypress in the precinct.
idiomatic: The burial was to take place in Changshan Commandery, where a shrine to Dong Zhuo already stood, with a cypress tree on the grounds.

literal: Langen held that Zhuo had been impious and lawless and ought not to have a shrine surviving to this day; he felled the cypress for coffin timber.
idiomatic: Langen held that Dong Zhuo, wicked and lawless, ought not to have a shrine surviving to the present. He felled the cypress for coffin timber.

literal: Some urged him not to cut it down; Langen took all he could, without the least fear.
idiomatic: Some urged him not to cut the tree; Langen took all he needed without the least fear.

literal: When his father died he built a hut by the tomb, carried earth to form the mound, and in grief nearly destroyed himself.
idiomatic: When his father died he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to mound the grave, grieving until he nearly destroyed himself.

literal: Later he served as recorder in the offices of the Minister of Works and Minister Over the Masses, transferred to chief clerk of the Pingbei headquarters in Xia Province, entered service as staff officer to the Minister Over the Masses, went out as Administrator of his home commandery — in all posts he showed competence in office.
idiomatic: Later he served as recorder in the offices of the minister of works and minister over the masses, became chief clerk of the pingbei headquarters in Xia Province, entered service as staff officer to the minister over the masses, and went out as administrator of his home commandery — proving competent in every post.

literal: At the end of Zhenguang, Minister of Works Li Chong was made Regional Commander of the commandery and led forces against the Rouran, with Langen as chief clerk.
idiomatic: At the end of Zhenguang, Minister of Works Li Chong was made regional commander of the commandery and led forces against the Rouran, with Langen as his chief clerk.

literal: Accordingly he said to Chong: "The garrisons along the frontier, controlling and overseeing distant regions.
idiomatic: He thereupon said to Li Chong: "The frontier garrisons were meant to control distant borders.

literal: When first established, the land was broad and the people sparse; some drew on strong clan sons from the interior, some were the state's own flesh and blood, entrusted as claws and fangs.
idiomatic: When first established, the land was broad and people sparse. Some drew strong clan sons from the interior; some were the state's very flesh and blood, posted as its claws and teeth.

literal: In mid-years the supervising offices departed from the facts; styled 'garrison households,' their labor was the same as bond-servants'; official marriage by roster caused loss of the clear stream.
idiomatic: In later years the supervising offices lost touch with reality. Called 'garrison households,' they were worked like bond-servants; official marriage-by-roster drove them from the gentry.

literal: Yet the old stock of each clan remained in glory one and all; looking back and forth at one another, indignation was only natural.
idiomatic: Yet each clan's original kin still rose to glory — and seeing the contrast, resentment was inevitable.

literal: To re-tune the zither and lute — the time is now; to quiet the borders and pacify the frontier is the greatest affair.
idiomatic: To re-tune policy — the time is now. Quieting the borders is the greatest task of state.

literal: It is fitting to change garrisons into provinces, divide and set up commanderies and counties; all who are garrison households should be freed as commoners, entering office by the order of precedence, all according to their former standard — employing civil and military together, majesty and grace alike.
idiomatic: Replace the garrisons with provinces and establish commanderies and counties. Free every garrison household as a commoner, restore them to their former place in office — use civil and military together, majesty and grace alike.

literal: If this plan is carried out, the state may be spared the worry of looking north.
idiomatic: If this plan prevails, the state may be spared constant watch to the north."

literal: Chong reported it up to Qin; the matter rested without response.
idiomatic: Chong reported upward; the proposal died in the bureaucracy.

literal: When the army returned, he was made General Who Wins Every Battle, transferred to senior clerk on the right of the Minister Over the Masses, with ceremonial staff, conducting the affairs of Yu Province.
idiomatic: When the army returned, he was made general who wins every battle, then senior clerk on the right of the minister over the masses, with ceremonial staff, conducting affairs of Yu Province.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he transferred to Inspector of Qi Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaochang he transferred to inspector of Qi Province.

literal: Following Mobile Headquarters Xiao Baoyin, he defeated Wanchuan; the captive populace were made slaves and bondmaids, and ten fair women were awarded to Langen as reward.
idiomatic: Following Mobile Headquarters Xiao Baoyin, he helped defeat Wanchuan. Captives were made slaves; ten fair women were awarded to Langen as his prize.

literal: Langen declined, saying: "This county borders strong enemies; imperial majesty has not yet reached here, and there was nowhere to turn — hence they rebelled.
idiomatic: Langen declined, saying, "This county borders strong enemies. Imperial authority had not yet reached them; with nowhere to turn, they rebelled.

literal: Now those who are cold should be clothed, those who hunger should be fed — how can we make them bond-servants?
idiomatic: Those who are cold should be clothed and those who hunger fed — how can we turn them into bond-servants?"

literal: He returned them all to their fathers and elder brothers.
idiomatic: He returned them all to their fathers and elder brothers.

literal: Within his district wheat often bore five ears; in neighboring provinces field mice brought disaster, but the plague's fangs did not enter Qi territory.
idiomatic: In his district wheat often bore five ears on one stalk; neighboring provinces suffered field-mouse plagues, but the blight did not cross into Qi territory.

literal: As Qin and Long rebelled, Xiao Baoyin was defeated at Jing Province; barbarian bandits of Gaoping pressed Qi Province, and the townsfolk forced and imprisoned Langen to surrender to the rebels.
idiomatic: When Qin and Long rose in rebellion, Xiao Baoyin was defeated at Jing Province. Gaoping barbarian bandits pressed Qi Province, and townsfolk forced Langen into captivity to surrender to the rebels.

literal: Baoyin reached Yong Province, gathered scattered troops, and military prestige revived; the townsfolk again beheaded the rebel inspector Hou Mo-Chen Zhonghe and urged Langen to resume his post.
idiomatic: Baoyin reached Yong Province, gathered scattered troops, and military prestige revived. The townsfolk beheaded the rebel inspector Hou Mo-Chen Zhonghe and urged Langen to resume office.

literal: The court, because Langen had won western hearts, additionally granted him ceremonial staff, made him provisional General Who Pacifies the West, supervisor of military affairs in the four provinces of Jing, Qi, Eastern Qin, and Southern Qi, and concurrently Mobile Headquarters Master of Writing for the four provinces.
idiomatic: Because Langen had won the hearts of the western territories, the court granted him ceremonial staff, made him provisional general who pacifies the west, supervisor of military affairs in Jing, Qi, Eastern Qin, and Southern Qi, and concurrent mobile headquarters master of writing for the four provinces.

literal: Soon he entered court and was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: Soon he entered court and was appointed grand master for splendid happiness.

literal: At the end of Xiaochang, refugees from Hebei crossed south; Langen was made concurrent Master of Writing and sent to pacify Qi, Ji, and the two Yan provinces, also establishing commanderies and counties.
idiomatic: At the end of Xiaochang, refugees from Hebei crossed south. Langen was made concurrent master of writing and sent to pacify Qi, Ji, and the two Yan provinces, establishing commanderies and counties as he went.

literal: Xing Gao of Hejian rebelled between Qing and Yan; Gao was Langen's sister's son, and again an edict ordered Langen to bear credentials and offer consolation.
idiomatic: Xing Gao of Hejian rebelled between Qing and Yan. Gao was Langen's nephew by marriage, and again an edict ordered Langen to bear credentials and reassure him.

literal: Gao would not submit; he thereupon followed Yuan Tianmu to campaign against him.
idiomatic: Gao would not submit; Langen thereupon followed Yuan Tianmu to campaign against him.

literal: On return he was made Grand Director of the Imperial Storeroom but declined the appointment and did not accept.
idiomatic: On return he was made grand director of the imperial storeroom but declined and did not accept.

literal: He transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Master of Writing in the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He transferred to general who pacifies the east and master of writing in the secretariat.

literal: As Emperor Zhuang was about to execute Erzhu Rong, Langen heard of the plan and secretly informed Erzhu Shilong.
idiomatic: As Emperor Zhuang was about to execute Erzhu Rong, Langen heard of the plan and secretly informed Erzhu Shilong.

literal: When Rong died, Langen feared the emperor would learn of it and was anxious, not knowing what course to take.
idiomatic: When Rong died, Langen feared Zhuang would learn of his involvement and was anxious, not knowing what to do.

literal: At the time, Attendant Respondant to Edicts Wang Daoxi enjoyed Zhuang's trust; Langen attached himself to him, seeking to win merit abroad.
idiomatic: At the time Wang Daoxi, attendant respondant to edicts, enjoyed Zhuang's trust. Langen attached himself to him, seeking merit in the field.

literal: Daoxi memorialized on his behalf; Langen was thereupon made Hebei Mobile Headquarters Commissioner, recruiting local levies at Ding Province, intending to guard Jingxing Pass.
idiomatic: Daoxi memorialized on his behalf, and Langen was made Hebei mobile headquarters commissioner, recruiting local levies in Ding Province to guard Jingxing Pass.

literal: At the time Erzhu Rong's general Hou Shen advanced from Fanyang toward Zhongshan; Langen fought him and was greatly defeated, fleeing to join Bohai Gao Gan.
idiomatic: At the time Erzhu Rong's general Hou Shen advanced from Fanyang toward Zhongshan. Langen fought him, was routed, and fled to join Gao Gan of Bohai.

literal: As the Gan brothers raised the righteous banner, he was among them.
idiomatic: When the Gan brothers raised the righteous banner, he was among them.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor arrived, because of Langen's long-standing repute he treated him with deep courtesy.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan arrived, he treated Langen with deep courtesy because of his long-standing repute.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was additionally made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was additionally made grand general of chariots and cavalry and right vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor was about to enter Luoyang, he dispatched Langen ahead to the capital.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan was about to enter Luoyang, he sent Langen ahead to the capital.

literal: As deposition and enthronement were not yet decided, he ordered Langen to observe the Wei Former Deposed Emperor.
idiomatic: As deposition and enthronement were still undecided, he ordered Langen to observe the Wei Former Deposed Emperor.

literal: The emperor's spirit and bearing were lofty and bright; Langen feared he would be hard to fathom later, and thereupon joined the Gan brothers and Yellow Gate Cui Juan in a united plea to the Grand Ancestor, saying the deposed emperor had originally been promoted by barbarian bandits, and that to install him again would not accord with reason.
idiomatic: The emperor's bearing was lofty and bright; Langen feared he would prove hard to control later. He joined the Gan brothers and Cui Juan of the yellow gate in pressing Gao Huan: the deposed emperor had been set up by barbarian rebels — to restore him would not be just.

literal: The Grand Ancestor, having no choice, thereupon enthroned Emperor Wucheng.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, with no choice, thereupon enthroned Emperor Wucheng.

literal: The deposed emperor had long possessed virtue and achievement, yet because Langen and others framed and defamed him, he was deeply censured by contemporary opinion.
idiomatic: The deposed emperor had long possessed virtue and achievement, yet Langen and others framed and defamed him — and were deeply censured by contemporary opinion.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators, soon additionally Opener of a Government Office, enfeoffed Marquis of Julu County with a fief of seven hundred households.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was made equal in protocol to three imperators, soon additionally opener of a government office, and enfeoffed marquis of Julu County with seven hundred households.

literal: He memorialized to grant his elder brother's son Tongda a share.
idiomatic: He memorialized to grant his elder brother's son Tongda a portion of the fief.

literal: Langen, having participated in the righteous merit, held a place at the tip of the scale; only then did he record the Qi Province merit and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongxing with a fief of one thousand households.
idiomatic: Having shared in the founding merit and now at the summit of office, Langen at last had his Qi Province service recognized and was enfeoffed marquis of Yongxing with one thousand households.

literal: When Gao Gan died, Langen was afraid, left his residence, and took refuge in a monastery.
idiomatic: When Gao Gan died, Langen took fright, left his house, and took refuge in a monastery.

literal: Emperor Wucheng severely condemned him; Langen, in terror, thereupon cited illness and resigned the vice directorship.
idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng severely condemned him. Langen, terrified, cited illness and resigned as vice director.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping, gravely ill, he submitted a memorial asking to return to his home district.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, gravely ill, he memorialized asking to return home.

literal: The Wei emperor sent Gentleman of the Household Shi Changxuan to visit his home with imperial consolation; he still held opener-of-office protocol, and his gate was accorded the display of posting horses — then he returned to his native place.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent Gentleman of the Household Shi Changxuan to visit his home with imperial consolation. He still held opener-of-office protocol and the gate display of posting horses, then returned to his native place.

literal: In the second year he died, aged sixty-one.
idiomatic: In the second year he died, aged sixty-one.

literal: Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in the three provinces of Ji, Ding, and Yin, Inspector of Ding Province, Duke over the Masses, Palace Attendant, with posthumous title Wenzuan.
idiomatic: Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Yin provinces, inspector of Ding Province, duke over the masses, and palace attendant, with the posthumous title Wenzuan.

literal: Though Langen established himself by merit and renown, he was skilled at attaching himself to power; in advancing and withdrawing he often put calculation first — hence he was not approved by pure opinion.
idiomatic: Though Langen had risen by merit, he was skilled at trimming to circumstance; in advancing and withdrawing he often calculated first — and was not approved by men of pure judgment.

literal: His eldest son Xiangru was a gentleman in the Secretariat.
idiomatic: His eldest son Xiangru served as gentleman in the secretariat.

literal: For Jianyi merit he was soon additionally made a general.
idiomatic: For Jianyi merit he was soon additionally made a general.

literal: He inherited his father's enfeoffment, was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and chief clerk in Yin Province, entered as Attending Censor.
idiomatic: He inherited his father's enfeoffment, became general who pacifies the east and chief clerk in Yin Province, and entered court as attending censor.

literal: He died in the third year of Wuding.
idiomatic: He died in the third year of Wuding.

literal: The second son Jingzhong.
idiomatic: His second son was Jingzhong.

literal: In Emperor Suzong's time, merit-holders who assisted at the founding were granted companion sacrifice, but Langen was not included.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong, founding merit-holders were granted temple companionship — but Langen was not included.

literal: Jingzhong submitted a petition; the emperor, because the edict had already been issued, found it hard to revise, but promoted Jingzhong to gentleman in the Ministry of Rites.
idiomatic: Jingzhong petitioned; the emperor, because the edict had already gone forth, found revision difficult but promoted Jingzhong to gentleman in the Ministry of Rites.

literal: He died as Administrator of Zhangwu.
idiomatic: He died while serving as administrator of Zhangwu.

literal: Langen's clansman Minglang had some acquaintance with the classics and histories and a rough literary bent.
idiomatic: Langen's clansman Minglang had some learning in the classics and histories and a rough literary bent.

literal: He was promoted repeatedly to legal bureau clerk in the Grand Marshal's office and concurrently gentleman in the Gold Section of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to legal bureau clerk in the grand marshal's office and concurrently gentleman in the gold section of the masters of writing.

literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Minglang was southern route mobile headquarters attendant and was captured by Hao.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Minglang was attendant on the southern route mobile headquarters and was captured.

literal: Later he abandoned Hao and fled back, was made General of Nimble Cavalry and Regular Grand Master, and granted the noble rank Marquis of Julu.
idiomatic: Later he abandoned Hao and fled back, was made general of nimble cavalry and regular grand master, and granted the noble rank marquis of Julu.

literal: At the end of Yong'an, Langen was Hebei mobile headquarters commissioner and brought in Minglang as left aide.
idiomatic: At the end of Yong'an, when Langen was Hebei mobile headquarters commissioner, he brought in Minglang as left aide.

literal: When Langen was defeated at Zhongshan, both returned to the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: When Langen was defeated at Zhongshan, both returned to Gao Huan.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made General Who Pacifies the Army and went out as Administrator of Ande.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made general who pacifies the army and went out as administrator of Ande.

literal: Later he transferred to Guard General, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Great Arbiter of Ding Province.
idiomatic: Later he became guard general, right grand master for splendid happiness, and great arbiter of Ding Province.

literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was Xianzu's advisory staff officer.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuding he was advisory staff officer to Gao Yang.

literal: He went out as Administrator of Pingyang, was impeached by the censor, and thereupon was detained.
idiomatic: He went out as administrator of Pingyang, was impeached by the censor, and was detained.

literal: He encountered illness and died.
idiomatic: He fell ill and died.

literal: Minglang's younger clansman Kai, in youth upright and outspoken, had talent for debate.
idiomatic: Minglang's younger clansman Kai was from youth upright and outspoken, with a gift for debate.

literal: At the end of Wei he was recruited as mobile headquarters attendant, and gradually rose to Master of Writing and chief clerk in Qi Province.
idiomatic: At the end of Wei he was recruited as mobile headquarters attendant and gradually rose to master of writing and chief clerk of Qi Province.

literal: In Tianbao he was deputy envoy on a mission to Chen.
idiomatic: In Tianbao he served as deputy envoy on a mission to Chen.

literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of Qing Province and firmly declined to take up the post.
idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk of Qing Province and firmly declined.

literal: Yang Yin reported it; Xianzu flew into a rage and said to Yin: "What sort of Han fellow is this — I give him office and he will not take it!
idiomatic: Yang Yin reported it. Gao Yang flew into a rage and told Yin, "What sort of fellow is this — I offer him office and he refuses!

literal: Tomorrow when he passes by, I will speak with him myself.
idiomatic: Tomorrow when he passes by, I will speak with him myself."

literal: At the time Xianzu had already lost virtue; the court all feared for Kai, yet Kai's manner and expression were calm.
idiomatic: By then Gao Yang had already lost restraint; the whole court feared for Kai, yet his bearing stayed calm.

literal: Xianzu sharply rebuked him and then said: "Death or the chief clerk's post — which is better? Choose whichever you like.
idiomatic: Gao Yang sharply rebuked him, then said, "Death or the chief clerk's post — which is better? Choose as you will."

literal: Kai replied: "He who can kill your servant is Your Majesty; he who refuses the chief clerk's post is your foolish servant — I await your clear command.
idiomatic: Kai replied, "He who can kill me is Your Majesty; he who refuses the chief clerk's post is your foolish servant. I await your clear command."

literal: Xianzu said to Yin: "Why worry that no one will fill offices — why use this fellow? Let him return home and never recall him.
idiomatic: Gao Yang said to Yin, "Why fear that no one will fill offices — why bother with this fellow? Let him go home and never recall him."

literal: Thereby for many years he sank into oblivion.
idiomatic: Thereby he sank into obscurity for many years.

literal: Later he encountered Yang Yin on the road and briefly opened his heart.
idiomatic: Later he met Yang Yin on the road and briefly unburdened himself.

literal: Yang replied: "Edicts granting office all issue from the sacred command — the selection bureau does not know of this; you need not trouble yourself with appeals.
idiomatic: Yang replied, "Edicts granting office issue from the throne — the selection bureau knows nothing of it. You need not appeal to me."

literal: Kai answered on the spot: "Though the scattered rain comes from heaven, in the end one must wait for clouds to rise from the four peaks.
idiomatic: Kai answered at once, "Though the scattered rain comes from heaven, in the end one must wait for clouds to rise from the four peaks.

literal: How can you say you do not know?
idiomatic: How can you say you do not know?"

literal: Yang said with delight: "These words are extremely concise — no more need be said.
idiomatic: Yang said with delight, "Those words are perfectly apt — no more need be said."

literal: Within several days he was made Inspector of Huo Province.
idiomatic: Within days he was made inspector of Huo Province.

literal: In office he had methods of governance and won the submission of border people.
idiomatic: In office he governed effectively and won the border people's trust.

literal: In Daning he died as Inspector of Jiao Province.
idiomatic: In the Daning era he died while serving as inspector of Jiao Province.

literal: Kai's younger clansman Yanqing was son of Wei Grand Director of the Imperial Granary Ji Jing.
idiomatic: Kai's younger clansman Yanqing was son of Wei grand director of the imperial granary Ji Jing.

literal: In Wuping he was concurrently Regular Attendant for the Palace in Direct Service on Imperial Dispatch, deputy envoy on a mission to Chen.
idiomatic: In Wuping he was concurrently regular attendant for the palace in direct service on imperial dispatch, deputy envoy to Chen.

literal: Yanqing's younger brother Tan, learned and with literary talent.
idiomatic: Yanqing's younger brother Tan was learned and had a gift for letters.
